description: This is a category, not one bag. Gucci has put a belt/waist bag (the fanny-pack silhouette worn at the hip or crossbody) into most of its house lines, so the name covers many models. You will see it in GG Marmont matelassé, Ophidia GG Supreme with the Web stripe, and plain GG canvas, in a few sizes. Which one you have depends on the print, hardware, and closure, so check those to pin down the actual model.

The Serpenti Forever is Bulgari's flap-bag line, closed by the jeweler's signature snakehead clasp with enamel scales and gemstone eyes. It draws on Bulgari's Serpenti motif, a snake design the house has worked since 1948 in jewelry. Bulgari's first Serpenti leather bags arrived in 2011; the Forever flap became the everyday face of the line, offered with interchangeable straps. Sourcing on the exact year the 'Forever' name was first used is thin, so we date it to the 2011 bag launch, not the name.
note: Single line; 2011 is the Serpenti handbag debut overall.

description: The Prada triangle is the house's logo, an enameled metal triangle plaque, and it names a family of bags rather than one model. Resellers use 'Triangle' for the small leather bags built around that plaque, including a mini shoulder bag and a hard triangle-shaped clutch. It sits alongside the Re-Nylon pieces that carry the same badge. Check the shape and material to identify the specific style.
note: MOTIF/LOGO FAMILY, not one canonical model.

description: Neo Vintage is a Gucci line, not one bag. It reworks the archival GG Supreme look, a beige-on-tan coated canvas with brown leather trim and a retro Gucci logo tag, across several shapes. The range includes messengers, crossbodies, double-zip bags, belt bags, and totes. So the name points to the material-and-mood family; the shape tells you the specific piece.

The Kelly To Go is Hermès's wallet-on-strap take on the Kelly, a long wallet dressed with the Kelly's turn-lock flap and sangle, worn crossbody or clutched. Hermès introduced its To Go wallet line in 2020. Collectors line it up against the Constance To Go and, in spirit, the Chanel Wallet on Chain. It carries a real Kelly's hardware at a smaller footprint.

The Soft Trunk is Virgil Abloh's reimagining of the Louis Vuitton trunk as a soft, wearable bag, debuted for his Spring-Summer 2019 show, his first collection for the house. It keeps the trunk's S-lock and corner lines but drops the rigid case, usually in Monogram or Monogram Eclipse canvas. It runs from the Mini up through larger messenger sizes. It was one of the few genuinely new silhouettes Abloh created for LV.

Pearl Crush is Chanel's name for the mini flaps fitted with an adjustable chain that loops through a large faux-pearl ball, so you can shorten the strap and let the pearl sit as a jewelry detail. It shows up mainly on the Mini Rectangular and Square flaps in lambskin. The pearl-ball adjuster is the tell. On the exact debut season our sourcing is thin, so read the year off the serial rather than trusting the market name.
note: DESIGN DETAIL/RECURRING NAME on mini flaps, not a standalone model.

description: The Brea is a discontinued Louis Vuitton top-handle satchel, a structured two-handle shape with a rolled top trim and a detachable strap. It's best known in Epi leather and also turned up in Vernis. It appears to date to around 2010, but that year rests on reseller and collector accounts rather than a house record, so treat it as approximate. Louis Vuitton no longer makes it, so it's a resale-only bag now.

New Wave is a Louis Vuitton line from the Fall/Winter 2018 collection, a softer, sportier look built on quilted, wave-embossed calfskin with a chunky chain-and-leather strap and a bright LV plaque. It runs across a chain bag, a camera bag, and totes. The read at the time was that it was Louis Vuitton's answer to the quilted-chain crowd like the GG Marmont. It's a leather line, distinct from the house's canvas classics.

The Stark is MCM's signature backpack, most recognizable in the brand's Visetos monogram-coated canvas with pyramid or side studs and nappa leather trim. It comes in mini through medium sizes and both studded and plain versions. It was one of the bags that carried MCM's logo-backpack moment in the mid-2010s. On the exact launch year our sourcing is thin, so we're leaving it unset rather than guessing.
note: Single named model; debut year not cleanly sourced.

description: Emblem points to Gucci's GG Emblem collection, a line of bags and small leather goods built around a bold Double G logo emblem rather than one single bag. Gucci frames it as a reinterpretation of its iconic motifs across new shapes. So the name is the badge and the capsule, not a specific silhouette. Check the shape and hardware to identify the exact piece.
note: COLLECTION/MOTIF, not a single model; overlaps Interlocking-G family.

description: Macadam is Celine's monogram-canvas print, a repeating C pattern the house has used since the early 1970s, not a single bag. It named an era of vintage Celine, most famously the coated-canvas Boston bags, totes, and shoulder bags. So a 'Celine Macadam' bag is defined by the print, with the shape naming the actual model. It reads as classic vintage Celine and is a common fake target, so authenticate carefully.
note: PRINT/MOTIF from the early 1970s, spans shapes.

description: The Vanity is Nicolas Ghesquière's take on Louis Vuitton's vanity case, a compact structured box bag with a top handle and, on later versions, a chain strap. It debuted at the Spring-Summer 2020 show, previewed by the house in October 2019, in Monogram and Monogram Reverse canvas, and later in leather. It comes mainly in the small PM size. It reworks the old cosmetics case into an everyday city bag.
note: Single model; distinct from vintage LV vanity cases.

description: Urban Essentials is a recent seasonal Chanel release tied to Matthieu Blazy's tenure, seen in a canvas shopping/tote shape with a reinforced base. Like most seasonal Chanel, it carries no permanent house model name, so 'Urban Essentials' functions as a market label, and the canonical identity is the style code plus season on the serial. Confirm any specific bag by its style code and season rather than the name.
note: SEASONAL Chanel; no official permanent name.

description: This is a Gucci GG Supreme line named for its retro-style Interlocking G buckle or emblem, not a single bag. It's rendered in the beige-and-tan GG Supreme canvas with leather trim across shoulder bags, crossbodies, and backpacks. So the name describes the logo hardware and the material family; the shape identifies the model. It sits in the same vintage-leaning GG Supreme world as Neo Vintage.
note: COLLECTION/MOTIF, spans shapes; overlaps Emblem/Neo Vintage.
